title: Temperaments
intro: A temperament adjusts ('tempers') some pure intervals so the rest fit. Meantone favoured pure thirds, well temperaments made every key usable with different colours, and equal temperament made every key the same.

blocks.text: Renaissance and early Baroque keyboards narrowed every fifth by a quarter of the syntonic comma (about 5.4 cents, to 696.6 cents) so that four fifths make a pure major third. Triads in the common keys sound sweet, but the circle does not close: one fifth (usually G♯–E♭) is a wolf of about 737.6 cents, 35.7 cents wider than pure, and keys with many sharps or flats are unusable. Some instruments had split keys (separate G♯ and A♭).

In the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, tunings by Werckmeister, Kirnberger, Vallotti and others spread the comma unevenly: the fifths near C are tempered most, so C, G and F have nearly pure thirds, while the fifths among the remote keys are pure, leaving their thirds wider. Every key is usable and each has its own colour. Whether Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier was meant for such a tuning or for equal temperament is still debated.

Twelve-tone equal temperament (12-TET) makes every semitone $2^{1/12}$. Every key is identical, enharmonic notes are the same, and music can modulate anywhere. The cost: no interval except the octave is pure. Fifths are 2 cents narrow (barely audible), but major thirds are 13.7 cents wide and beat quickly. It became the standard piano tuning during the nineteenth century.

Other numbers of equal steps approximate pure intervals differently. The plot shows the error of the best step for the fifth, the major third and the harmonic seventh (7/4) in each division from 5 to 60:

widget.title: How well n equal steps approximate pure intervals

items: 19: third −7.4, fifth −7.2. Close to third-comma meantone; enharmonics are different notes (C♯ ≠ D♭).
31: third +0.8, fifth −5.2, seventh −1.1. Almost exactly quarter-comma meantone; Huygens proposed it in 1691, and Fokker built a 31-tone organ in 1950.
53: fifth −0.07, third −1.4 cents. Practically just and Pythagorean at once; used in theory of Turkish makam music.
24 (quarter tones): the 12-TET intervals plus intervals halfway between, used in Arabic maqam theory.

blocks.title: Meantone fifth
blocks.text: Show that narrowing each fifth by 1/4 of the syntonic comma makes four fifths a pure major third (plus two octaves).
solution: Four pure fifths overshoot 5/4 (plus two octaves) by one syntonic comma, 81/80. Narrowing each by a quarter comma removes the whole comma: 4 × (701.955 − 21.506/4) = 2807.82 − 21.51 = 2786.31 cents = 2400 + 386.31, and 386.31 cents is exactly 5/4.

blocks.title: Which division
blocks.text: Using the error formula (round the interval to the nearest step of 1200/n), find the error of the major third in 22-EDO.
solution: 5/4 = 386.31 cents. One step of 22-EDO = 54.55 cents. 386.31 / 54.55 = 7.08, so the nearest step is 7: 381.82 cents. Error = 381.82 − 386.31 = −4.5 cents.
